title: Application of large volume injection for sensitive LC-MS/MS analysis of seven artificial sweeteners in surface waters
author: Henschel, Hayen

steps.title: Configure HPLC system and column
steps.instruction: Install the Kaseisorb LC ODS‑SAX Super column (150 × 2.0 mm, 3.0 µm; TCI) on the Agilent 1100 series HPLC, set the column temperature to 40 °C and the mobile‑phase flow rate to 0.25 mL min⁻¹.

steps.title: Prepare mobile phases
steps.instruction: Make mobile‑phase A by dissolving ammonium formate to a final concentration of 20 mM and adjusting the pH to 3.5; mobile‑phase B is acetonitrile (ACN). Mix them to give an initial composition of 85 % A : 15 % B (v/v).

steps.title: Program gradient for mixed‑mode separation
steps.instruction: Set a two‑step gradient: start with 15 % ACN (mobile‑phase B) from 0 to 5 min, then increase to 40 % ACN, and finally to 80 % ACN as illustrated in Fig. 2. Maintain the initial 85 % A : 15 % B composition before the gradient begins.

steps.title: Load sample and set injection volume
steps.instruction: Connect the Agilent multidraw upgrade kit (400 µL extension) and the 100 µL sample loop to the HPLC. Begin with a 10 µL injection to verify system performance, then perform large‑volume injections (LVI) of 500 µL of the surface‑water sample, allowing refocusing at the column head.

steps.title: Configure mass spectrometer source
steps.instruction: Set the EVOQ Elite™ triple‑quadrupole (Bruker) to positive/negative switching mode, apply a heated electrospray voltage of ±4000 V, set cone and heated‑probe temperature to 350 °C, and adjust gas flows to: cone gas 20 units, probe gas 40 units, nebulizer gas 60 units.

steps.title: Run LC‑MS/MS analysis
steps.instruction: Start the LC gradient, inject the 500 µL sample, and acquire data using the programmed MRM transitions in positive/negative switching mode. Use Compass Hystar 4.0 and MS Workstation (Bruker) for instrument control, data acquisition, and evaluation.
